stories.author: _da_
stories.title: App Store Rejection of the Week: Dark Hours
stories.groq_label: Apple rejects Dark Hours, an astronomy app, citing astrology reasons based on a non-existent tarot reading feature.
stories.groq_discussion:
Discussion type: – Short:

This App Store rejection of Dark Hours is centered around the inclusion of a live reading feature, which the Review Board mistakenly identified as a tarot reading feature. Commenters generally view this as an example of the Byzantine App Store bureaucracy and an insane ruling. Many praised React Native and over-the-air updates as a way to avoid dealing with this kind of uncertainty. The discussion also touched on the broader issue of App Store gatekeeping and the potential for inconsistent reviews. The overall sentiment is cautious and critical of the App Store process.
stories.groq_explain: A developer, Terry Godier, created an iOS app for astronomy called Dark Hours, but it was rejected by Apple's App Store because they thought it was about astrology, even though it contains a feature unrelated to astrology - a live tarot reading function. The app was eventually rejected with the excuse that it includes tarot reading, which isn't even related to astrology, and wasn't an honest mistake. This matters because it shows a lack of understanding and reason in the app review process, making it difficult for developers like Godier to get their high-quality apps approved and showcased on the App Store.
